I'm using the fuzzy search algorithm from https://github.com/mattyork/fuzzy. Here's the gdscript which is extremely ugly because I couldn't be bother make it better :sweat_smile:
GDScript implementation

```gdscript class Fuzzy: static func score(pattern: String, str:String, hits: Array) -> float: pattern = pattern.to_lower() str = str.to_lower() if str == pattern: return INF var total_score = 0 var cur_score = 0 var pattern_idx = 0 var pattern_len = pattern.length() for i in str.length(): if pattern_idx < pattern_len and pattern[pattern_idx] == str[i]: pattern_idx += 1 cur_score += 1 + cur_score hits.append(i) else: cur_score = 0 total_score += cur_score if pattern_idx == pattern_len and str == pattern: total_score = INF return total_score static func fuzzy_search(query: String, items: Array[Dictionary]) -> Array[Dictionary]: var result: Array[Dictionary] = [] for item in items: var hits = [] var str = item.get("item") var item_score = score(query, str, hits) result.append({ "item": str, "index": item.get("index"), "score": item_score, "hits": hits }) if query.length() > 2: result = result.filter(func(a): return a.score > 2) result.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a.score > b.score) return result ```

As it so happens I started working on exactly this feature, for godotengine/godot-proposals#3333, without realizing that this PR was already open and actively developed for a very similar proposal.

Unsurprisingly, the code ended up looking quite similar, given that we both just stuck a `LineEdit` next to the `ScrollContainer` inside a `VBoxContainer`. There were however a few differences, which I figured might be worth highlighting, in case there's any interest in bringing them over into this PR. You can find my (incomplete) attempt in #117020.

The notable differences (in no particular order) would seem to be:

1. I refer to it as "filter" instead of "search", which I would argue is more consistent with similar inputs found in the editor already.
1. I did not add anything equivalent to `enable_search_bar_on_item_count`, which I suppose could be useful, but at the same time I guess you can also just enable/disable the filter yourself based on the number of items you're adding.
1. I added fuzzy filtering using the existing `FuzzySearch` class, same as a lot of the other filter inputs in the editor. I did not make this configurable, but I suppose it should be.
1. I added the ability to always hide/show specific items from the filtering, which seemed useful for `EditorResourcePicker`. You can see it in action in [#117020](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117020).
1. I recalculate the "wrapped" size of the popup when the filter changes, but I keep the width, so as to avoid weird jank. I would argue this looks better in the editor at least, but it might be more controversial in the general case.
1. I tried to account for accessibility as best I could, which this PR does not seem to do, likely breaking screen readers and such. I was however not able to get next/previous focus actions to work well, so that still needs some work.
1. I used `grab_focus(false)` instead of `edit(true)`. I suppose `edit` is more correct, but I would probably argue we should not hide focus in this case, since the user isn't explicitly selecting the `LineEdit`, but I'm no expert on accessibility conventions.
1. I pre-select the top-most item when filtering, allowing you to just press Enter to select it. I'll admit this does not feel/look great when using a screen reader, since the focus is still on the `LineEdit`, but I would argue it's a must-have without one.
1. I did not add any icon, like you did, which looks great.
1. I reset the filter on `_pre_popup`, which seemed to make sense for `EditorResourcePicker`, but again might be controversial in the general case.
1. I refer to the visibility state as `hidden` instead of `visible`, which (while very nitpicky) would seem to line up better with the existing negative `Item::disabled`.

I'm probably missing some other important difference, but that's all I can spot right now. I'm sure there's a bug or two in mine that have already been fixed here as well.

I'm obviously quite invested in this now, so I'd be happy to help out here in any way I can. I would probably say the fuzzy searching is a no-brainer to port over, and I'm personally very keen on seeing the first filtered item being pre-selected, to allow for a quick submit/enter without needing to press the down arrow key first. Accessibility probably needs fixing as well, but maybe that can be done in a separate PR. The rest is more subjective I guess.

Excuse me, I’m wondering why the search bar not be displayed when the PopupMenu has a parent popup.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6d6e822c689acb54bf86e19cc2bbbe3fa567b123/scene/gui/popup_menu.cpp#L3635-L3643
@jinyangcruise My reasoning was recursive search. Since you can search items inside submenus, there's no need to provide search bars for submenus.

Got it. That sounds like a good idea. However, this behavior is governed by the `search_bar_enabled_on_item_count` setting of the parent popup. If the parent popup does not contain enough items to trigger the search bar, the search bar will not appear—even when the sub-popup menu has a large number of entries.

Additionally, your recursive search method checks the state of hidden sub-popups. However, the content within these sub-popups can be post-modified through the `about_to_popup` signal. This leaves developers using some workarounds, for instance, refresh submenu items via the parent menu’s `about_to_popup` callback, instead of using its own `about_to_popup` logic to handle item updates.

What if we let users decide? A new property such as `search_behavior` will be added. They can opt for :
1. Recursive search when their popup menu items are static (It remains necessary to fix the issue where submenu search is governed by the `search_bar_enabled_on_item_count` setting of its parent menu).
2. Enable the search bar for each individual popup menu based on its own item count.

There might be some better options out there.
